---
title: "OpticalPath"
sidebar: api
---

`OpticalPath` is the ordered optical-distance model used to project physical metadata onto DAS data. It is linked from a `FiberArray`, carries time validity, and can be operated on directly before being placed back into an `Inventory`.

## Path Operations

```python
from dascore.core.inventory import OpticalPath

path = fiber_array.optical_paths[0]

short_path = path.select(distance=(100.0, 500.0))
left, right = path.split_at(250.0)
reversed_path = path.reverse()
joined_path = left + right

path.validate()
```

`select(distance=(start, stop))` clips optical components, geometries, coupling conditions, and annotations to the requested optical-distance interval. Open bounds can use `None`. Selections and splits preserve absolute optical distances — pieces are never rebased to zero.

`split_at(distance)` returns the two selected path pieces on either side of the split distance.

`reverse()` reverses ordered tracks and rewrites every distance-bearing track — geometry arrays, coupling intervals, and annotations — against the reversed path.

`path_a + path_b` concatenates two paths when their CRS definitions match, rewriting the second path's tracks onto the combined axis.

`validate()` checks that the optical components tile the path's span — `[start_distance, start_distance + total component length)`, with `start_distance` 0 for whole paths and set by `select`/`split_at` on pieces — and that geometry, coupling, and annotation tracks stay within path bounds. Geometry and coupling coverage may be partial; uncovered intervals are undefined rather than invalid. Overlapping geometry segments or coupling conditions raise; annotations may overlap freely.

## Patch Projection

`Patch.enrich` resolves the valid optical path from the patch `data_source_id` and patch time, mapping channels to optical distance internally (via the acquisition's `distance_map` or affine form) before projecting the path tracks:

```python
patch = patch.enrich(
    inventory,
    coords=("distance", "labels", "x", "y", "z", "optical_components.name"),
    on_missing="nan",
)
```

Coordinate requests can include optical `distance` itself; geometry axes such as `x`, `y`, `z`, `latitude`, `longitude`, and `elevation`; annotation labels via the per-channel `labels` coord; and interval metadata from qualified tracks such as `optical_components.name`, `geometry.name`, `coupling.coupling_type`, or `annotations.label` (`labels` is the shorthand for the last). Qualified names match the model attributes (and the authoring CSV stems) exactly. Explicitly requesting `labels` raises where annotations overlap the requested channels; the general overlapping case belongs to `Spool.split_by_labels`. The blanket `coords=True` form includes `labels` only when the patch's channels are overlap-free and silently omits it otherwise — only an explicit request raises.

## Design Rule

`OpticalPath` is not the raw channel table: the [acquisition maps channels into optical distance](../Model/model.qmd); the path maps optical distance into geometry, annotations, coupling, and optical-component context.
